episode_title: The Wirehouse Exodus Myth: Why 57% of Departing Advisors Stayed W2

real_qa.q: What percentage of advisors departing wire houses stayed in W-2 employment in 2024?
real_qa.r: 57% of advisors that left a wire house or W-2 shop stayed in another W-2 channel, compared to 60% the previous year. About one-third, 36%, went independent. This shows that the majority of departing advisors remained within the W-2 model rather than transitioning to independence.

real_qa.q: How many advisors left wire house firms in 2024 year-to-date versus the previous year?
real_qa.r: In 2024 year-to-date as of end of September, 9% fewer advisors left the wire house space compared to the previous year when 1,444 advisors departed. The wire houses were losing less advisors, but simultaneously were recruiting 15% fewer experienced advisors: 713 versus 837 in January to August of the prior year.

real_qa.q: Which regional and W-2 firms are winning the most advisors departing from wire houses?
real_qa.r: Raymond James was noted as one of the big winners on the W-2 side. Other successful firms recruiting departing wire house advisors include Jannie, RBC, Oppenheimer, LPL's Linsco channel, JPMorgan (131 advisors), Wells Fargo (113 advisors), Morgan Stanley (107 advisors), and Raymond James (70 advisors). These firms are staying within the W-2 model while attracting wire house talent.
real_qa.requete: wire house advisors moving to Raymond James RBC Oppenheimer

real_qa.q: What is the hiring-to-attrition ratio at Rockefeller compared to other W-2 firms?
real_qa.r: Rockefeller loses one advisor for every 15 that they hire, demonstrating significantly lower attrition compared to other wire houses. In contrast, Merrill Lynch recruited only 141 advisors in the recent period compared to 300 the year before, and they hire six advisors for every 10 that they lose.

real_qa.q: Why are wire house firms recruiting fewer experienced advisors despite offering aggressive compensation deals?
real_qa.r: Wire house firms are recruiting 15% fewer experienced advisors year-over-year even with deals starting at four handles (400%+), because advisors are voting with their feet toward regional and alternative W-2 platforms. Firms like Raymond James and RBC offer more stable compensation plans that rarely change, whereas wire houses move compensation goalposts annually, requiring advisors to produce 10-15% more to maintain payout levels.
real_qa.requete: why wire houses losing advisors recruitment
